g.text: The feature, and the one ratio that decides the architecture
A mapping from a short code to a long URL. Everything hard about it is on the right.
The one thing that must never happen
One code, two destinations - and a user is silently sent to the wrong website.
There is no graceful degradation for a collision.
THEN · the same code is opened, again and again
That ratio is the entire reason a cache exists: it turns 116,000 reads/sec into about 5,800/sec reaching the
database. And the redirect must resolve in under 50ms at p99 - it is invisible latency inside someone else's
page load, so when it is slow, the DESTINATION site is what feels slow.
